newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end flat, surrender early gains.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end flat, surrender early gains.

text.p: The steam fizzled out of an early rally in Bombay stocks as lack of follow-up buying by major players saw prices close mixed in listless trade, dealers said.
"There are not many new buying orders from foreign funds. The market may take some time to adjust," said Kirti Doshi, dealer at Biyani Securities.

Market participants said Monday's nervous sell-off in share prices caused by a move by the regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) to quit India's minority coalition government attracted some bargain-hunting by foreign funds, but the market failed to hold on to its gains.
Political worries led the Bombay index to fall over two percent on Monday, its biggest fall since a 303-point tumble on March 30.
"The markets should stabilise around these levels," S. Gopalakrishnan, research head at UTI Securities, told Reuters.
The Bombay share index ended 4.92 points lower at a provisional 4,220.19.
"Funds left out in the rally could now join in." He said the lack of any major sales pressed by local funds was another factor that could push up share prices.
Short-covering by local operators on the last day of the weekly trade account at the National Stock Exchange helped the index close in positive territory on Tuesday, traders said.
Fresh political developments will continue to provide future stock market direction, dealers said.
"The market is dicey about the political situation," said Mehul Patel, trader at brokers Mukesh Babu. "Foreign funds were only select buyers. In the short-run, prices are expected to move sideways."

Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav, a breakaway group of Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party on Tuesday won a confidence vote in the eastern state of Bihar, state assembly officials said.
